[Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/) [reflects](https://simonwillison.net/2026/May/6/vibe-coding-and-agentic-engineering/) on his recent appearance on [Heavybit's High Leverage podcast](https://www.heavybit.com/library/podcasts/high-leverage/ep-9-the-ai-coding-paradigm-shift-with-simon-willison) and notices something uncomfortable: the line he drew between vibe coding and the responsible use of AI to write code, which he now calls *agentic engineering*, has started to blur in his own work. He no longer reviews every line of code [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code) writes for him, even on production systems, and he names the trust drift directly: normalization of deviance.

## What the post argues

- **Vibe coding and agentic engineering are blurring.** The hard line he once drew between them, where vibe coding doesn't look at the code and agentic engineering does, no longer holds in his own work. He's stopped reviewing every line Claude Code writes, even on production systems.
- **The internal-team analogy.** When another team hands him an image-resize service, he doesn't read its source. He reads the docs and ships, digging in only if something breaks. He's starting to treat coding agents the same way.
- **Normalization of deviance is the risk.** Every uninspected commit that turns out fine pushes trust up, and at some point he'll trust the agent at the wrong moment and get burned. Claude Code has no professional reputation to lose, which is what made the human-team analogy work in the first place.
- **Polished repos no longer signal quality.** A polished README, a hundred commits, and full tests used to mean weeks of care. It now takes half an hour. The new signal is whether someone has actually used the thing.
- **Bottlenecks shift upstream too.** Citing [Anthropic design leader Jenny Wen](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jan/24/dont-trust-the-process/): elaborate design processes exist because three-month build mistakes are catastrophic. If builds aren't three months anymore, the design process can be cheaper and riskier.
- **He's not afraid for his career.** Working with agents reminds him how hard software is. The tools amplify what an experienced engineer already knows. He'd rather use a professionally managed AI-assisted product than vibe-code his own. "I can plumb my house if I watch enough YouTube videos. I would rather hire a plumber."

## My Notes

Disasters strike when you stop watching. Trust accrued over a streak of clean commits doesn't immunize the next one. In late April, [a Cursor agent wiped a company's production database and Railway backups in nine seconds](/posts/20260427-cursor-railway-production-wipe/) and then enumerated, in writing, the safety rules it had violated. The defense against the long tail isn't more careful review — it's the harness and guardrails around the agent: sandboxes that can't reach production, write-fences on destructive commands, rollback paths that survive the agent's mistakes.
